news.title: Japan end Bangladesh’s unbeaten run, World Cup dream
news.lede: Bangladesh’s hopes of securing a place in the FIH Women’s Junior World Cup were dashed on Thursday as the women in red and green suffered a 2-0 defeat to Japan in the quarterfinals of the Women’s Junior Asia Cup in China. Bangladesh will now play a fifth-sixth place-deciding match against either Malaysia or South Korea. The top four teams in the tournament will qualify for the next edition of the Women’s Junior World Cup. The women in red and green entered the quarterfinals as unbeaten champions of the Challenger Pool, having won all four of their matches.

news.title: Dream Maker Gustavo Alfaro Extends Paraguay Contract Until 2030 World Cup
news.lede: Gustavo Alfaro will continue as the manager of the Paraguayan national football team until the conclusion of the 2030 FIFA World Cup. The announcement was made by Robert Harrison, president of the Paraguayan Football Association (APF), through the organisation’s social media channels. The Argentine coach has been pivotal in the recent success of the national team, known as the Albirroja. He successfully guided the squad to qualify for the 2026 World Cup, marking a significant achievement for the nation.

news.title: Football: Soccer-DR Congo's World Cup exploits encourage more players to join their cause
news.lede: Sept 12 (Reuters) - Democratic Republic of Congo's ⁠success at this year’s World Cup has seen a bevy of European-born players added to their squad as ⁠coach Sebastien Desabre seeks to expand the player pool and build on their last-32 place at the finals ‌in North America. DR Congo will later this month play their first matches since the World Cup, where they were 15 minutes away from an upset win over England in Atlanta, when they begin the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers. Six new players from European clubs have since been added to the ​squad to face Equatorial Guinea in Kinshasa on September 24 and Zimbabwe away ⁠in Harare four days later. Former Manchester United centre back ⁠Willy Kambwala, now at Italian club Como, was named along with Ezechiel Banzuzi (Leipzig), Stanis Idumbo (AS Monaco), Jordy Makengo (Freiburg), Noah Mbamba (Lorient) ⁠and ‌Kevin Pedro (Saint-Etienne).

news.title: Morocco PM rejects own football chief's 2030 World Cup final claim, asks him not to make promises | 'There should be some respect, brothers' | Inshorts
news.lede: Morocco's PM Aziz Akhannouch rebuked football federation chief Fouzi Lekjaa after he declared Benslimane would host 2030 World Cup final. 'Don't offer to host...big final game in Morocco while we still haven't ​discussed the matter with our allies, cohosts Spain and Portugal,' he said. Spanish FA president Rafael Louzan insisted the final 'cannot and mustn't' be held anywhere but Spain.

news.title: Morocco PM warns football chief over 2030 World Cup final
news.lede: Morocco’s Prime Minister, Aziz Akhannouch, has warned the country’s football federation president, Fouzi Lekjaa, against making promises about hosting the 2030 World Cup final before discussions with co-hosts Spain and Portugal. The 2030 men’s World Cup will be jointly hosted by Morocco, Spain and Portugal, with the opening three matches taking place in Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay as part of celebrations marking the tournament’s centenary. Although a proposed list of host stadiums has been drawn up, FIFA has yet to confirm the final venues or where the tournament’s showpiece match will be played. Lekjaa, president of the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (RMFF), had said at a political party event that Casablanca would have the “honour” of hosting the final.

news.title: Cristiano Ronaldo vs Lionel Messi: The FIFA World Cup Face-Off Fans Deserved but Never Got
news.lede: The greatest rivalry in football over the last two decades has been that of Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi. Because they played in the same era, the debate continues even now as to who the best player in the world is. Fans have clashed on this while the players have always spoken with respect when referring to one another. No FIFA World Cup ClashThe two have faced off at club level and occasionally in international friendlies.

news.title: Transplant recipients are set for Football World Cup in Frankfurt
news.lede: TRANSPLANT recipients from Tallaght, Newcastle and Crumlin are set to head off to Frankfurt and represent Ireland at the Transplant Football World Cup from Sunday. The Transplant Sport Ireland (TSI) team will join transplant recipients from around the world for the international seven-a-side tournament set to take place from this Sunday to Friday, September 18 at the grounds of FSV Frankfurt 1899, including their 12,500-capacity PSD Bank Arena. The full team is made up of ten Irish transplant recipients, including seriously ill people who once faced just weeks or months to live, and Tallaght’s James Reynolds, Newcastle’s Shane Riordan and Crumlin’s Brian Carney are among the squad’s talents.
